title: "Alien base or Noah's Ark?" - mysterious lights in the mountains of Almaty intrigued Kazakhstanis
excerpt: Unusual lights in the mountains near Almaty attracted the attention of Kazakhstanis. A photo taken by a plane passenger garnered more than 500,000 views on Threads. Users speculated that a secret base or even Noah's Ark could be located there. Tengri Life found out what kind of place it is.
content:
How it all began

The image was shared on social media by Daniyar, an Almaty resident. He explained that on November 16, he was flying home from Phu Quoc on flight DV-5321. About thirty minutes before landing, he noticed unusual lights nestled in the mountains.

"I was flying back to Almaty from vacation at night. About 30 minutes before landing, I saw these lights right in the middle of the mountains. Does anyone know what is located here, in the mountains near Almaty?" Daniyar wrote.

Screenshot: Threads

The post amassed more than 500,000 views. In the comments, Kazakhstanis began speculating and joking about what could be hidden inside the mysterious location.

"Maybe it's a crypto mining farm?", "That’s Noah’s Ark! The shape and size match perfectly," "It's a secret airfield. They're already on their way to get you," "Must be an alien base," social media users wrote.

Statement from the Akimat

We reached out to the Almaty Region Akimat (local administration). They clarified that there is no mystery: the lights belong to the village of Kalzhat in the Uygur District.

"The village of Kalzhat is located in the southeastern part of the Uygur District, at the foot of the Tien Shan Mountains, on the border with the People's Republic of China. It is 110 kilometers from the district center. The land area is 58,198 hectares, with a population of 2,315 people," the Akimat reported.

According to regional authorities, while the village has no historical or natural monuments, Kalzhat is famous for its orchards and fruit.

"The village grows apricots on 12.5 hectares, various apple varieties on 38 hectares, and walnuts on 0.07 hectares. Furthermore, a unique variety grows here—the Kalzhat apple—which, due to the area's natural characteristics, is found nowhere else," the Akimat stated.

Three rivers flow through the village territory—the Bodeti (Kyzyl Ova), Kasansai, and Kalzhatsai. To the east, Kalzhat sits just 7 kilometers from the Chinese border.

Today, Kalzhat consists of 641 residential homes and 758 families, with a total population of 2,315.
